subject.title: fix(browser): tab creation steals window focus during agent automation

question: Should OpenClaw's extension relay intentionally treat a fully omitted `Target.createTarget` background/focus request as background automation, diverging from native CDP's foreground default while preserving every explicit request?
rationale: The code and proof establish correctness, but source inspection cannot decide whether compatibility with native CDP omission semantics or non-disruptive OpenClaw automation is the permanent product contract.

options.title: Adopt background automation default
options.body: Accept the relay-specific omitted-parameter behavior because the endpoint serves OpenClaw automation and explicit CDP foreground and focus requests remain fully supported.

options.title: Preserve native CDP omission semantics
options.body: Keep omitted requests foreground and add a separate internal signal or creation path so only OpenClaw-owned automation requests background tabs.

recommendation.title: Adopt background automation default
recommendation.body: Accept the relay-specific omitted-parameter behavior because the endpoint serves OpenClaw automation and explicit CDP foreground and focus requests remain fully supported.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest ownership of browser client, CDP, route, and extension-relay behavior.
